terra-preta.name: Terra preta
terra-preta.summary: A dark, fertile soil found in the Amazon Basin, created by indigenous farmers mixing charcoal, bones, pottery and manure into naturally poor soil, and remaining fertile for thousands of years.

maraj.name: Marajó
maraj.summary: A large island in Pará, Brazil, at the mouth of the Amazon, site from roughly 400 BCE to 1600 CE of the advanced pre-Cabraline Marajoara society.

maloca.name: Maloca
maloca.summary: Traditional Amazonian long house shared by several families, with separate entrances for men and women and space cleared for ceremonial dances.

marajoara-culture.name: Marajoara culture
marajoara-culture.summary: An ancient culture that flourished on Marajó island at the mouth of the Amazon in Brazil, with human activity documented as early as 1000 BCE.

mapuche.name: Mapuche
mapuche.summary: An Indigenous people of south-central Chile and southwestern Argentina, with a traditional economy based on agriculture and material culture known for textiles and silverwork.

mapudungun.name: Mapudungun
mapudungun.summary: The language of the Mapuche people, spoken in south-central Chile and west-central Argentina, with no official national status in either country.

tau-mythology.name: Tau
tau-mythology.summary: An evil spirit in Guaraní mythology, created by the supreme god Tupã alongside his opposite, Angatupyry, and left with humanity on Earth.

s-o-raimundo-nonato.name: São Raimundo Nonato
s-o-raimundo-nonato.summary: A city in southern Piauí, Brazil, about 576 km from the capital Teresina, known as the location of the Serra da Capivara National Park.

minas-gerais.name: Minas Gerais
minas-gerais.summary: A landlocked Brazilian state in the Southeast Region, the fourth largest by area and second most populous, whose capital is Belo Horizonte.

acre-state.name: Acre
acre-state.summary: A state in western Brazil's Amazon region, historically shaped by an early-20th-century rubber boom that drew settlers from many parts of the country.
